what_it_does: Exfoliates the skin surface to smooth texture, brighten tone, and support even-looking skin.
summary_short: Glycolic acid is an alpha hydroxy acid used to exfoliate the skin and improve dullness, uneven texture, and discoloration. It has clinical support in chemical peels, especially for melasma, but it can irritate sensitive skin and increases the need for daily sunscreen.
summary_long:
Glycolic acid is an alpha hydroxy acid (AHA) used in skincare to loosen the bonds between dead surface skin cells. This helps speed up shedding of the outer layer of skin, which can make skin look smoother, brighter, and more even over time.

The strongest evidence in the provided abstracts comes from chemical peel research. A 2024 systematic review of chemical peels for melasma found that peels were generally safe and effective, and that glycolic acid was among the safest and most effective options for melasma treatment [PMID:unknown]. A broader review of superficial and medium-depth peels also notes that peel depth affects both results and complication risk [PMID:unknown].

For consumers, this means glycolic acid can be useful for uneven tone, rough texture, and visible sun-damage-related dullness, but stronger peel-style use is different from everyday leave-on skincare. Professional peels can give more noticeable results, but they also carry a higher risk of irritation, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, and barrier disruption when overused.

The main safety concern is irritation: stinging, redness, peeling, dryness, or sensitivity can happen, especially with sensitive skin or frequent use. Because exfoliation can make skin more vulnerable to sun-related irritation and discoloration, daily broad-spectrum sunscreen is especially important when using glycolic acid.

Glycolic acid is commonly paired with moisturizers, barrier-supporting ingredients, and sunscreen. It can be harder to tolerate when layered with other strong exfoliants, retinoids, or low-pH actives, so many people do better using those on alternate nights.
